title: Introducing Hyperbound Initiatives: see whether your rollout is landing on real calls
summary: Hyperbound Initiatives shows whether new messaging and skills land on real sales calls, and gives every rep who misses a moment feedback and practice. (
body_markdown:
*Hyperbound Initiatives, a system for autonomous behavior change, is now part of Hyperbound Perform, the part of Hyperbound's AI sales coaching platform that scores and analyzes your team's real sales calls. It shows enablement whether new messaging and skills are showing up on real calls, and gives every rep who misses a moment feedback and practice on it.*


‍


Every quarter, enablement teams ship something new: a pitch, a product launch, a battlecard, a methodology. Reps sit through the session. They pass the certification. The dashboard turns green.


Then the rollout disappears into a few thousand recorded calls that nobody has time to listen to.


A quarter later, someone asks whether the new messaging stuck. Nobody really knows. And by then, it's too late to do anything about it.


‍


‍


## The problem: rollouts fade, and nobody sees it happen


This isn't a hunch. In a March 2026 survey of 419 B2B revenue leaders,[Revenue Innovations](https://www.revenueinnovations.com/research/2026) found:


- **59%** of teams saw new sales behavior fade within 90 days of a methodology rollout.
- **1 in 10** were still applying it a year later.
- **79%** already run structured weekly or monthly reinforcement, and **58%** of those teams still saw the change fade inside 90 days. Ad hoc teams: 63%.
- On **four in ten** teams, leaders say frontline managers can't coach the method they were given.


One VP of Revenue Operations in that survey put it plainly: the biggest unsolved challenge is "driving consistent seller behavior change in real-world buyer situations."


The reinforcement calendar is already full. What's missing is visibility. The behavior lives on calls, and most calls are never heard by anyone but the rep and the buyer. Conversation intelligence vendors estimate that managers review[less than 1% of recorded calls](https://www.avoma.com/blog/sales-call-reviews) .


So enablement is left measuring the one thing it can see: who finished the training.


‍


## Hot take: certification is the most expensive vanity metric in sales


We'll say it: a completion rate tells you almost nothing about whether a rollout worked.


Certification proves a rep can say the right thing once, in a room with no buyer, no pressure and no deal on the line. It doesn't prove they'll say it on Tuesday's discovery call when the prospect pushes back. Yet completion rates are still the number most enablement teams bring to leadership, because they're the only number they can get.


That's not an enablement failure. It's a visibility failure. If you can't see what happens on real calls, you report what you can see.


The fix isn't more training or another reinforcement calendar. It's measuring the behavior where it actually happens, on real calls, while the rollout is still live, and acting on every miss before it becomes a habit.


Stop asking "who finished the training?" Start asking "who's doing it on calls?"


‍


## Introducing Hyperbound Initiatives


Today we're introducing Hyperbound Initiatives, a system for autonomous behavior change, now part of Hyperbound Perform, the part of Hyperbound that scores and analyzes your team's real sales calls.


Initiatives shows enablement whether every rollout is showing up on real calls, while it's happening. And every rep who misses a moment gets feedback and practice on that exact moment.


**How it works**


1. **Tell Kota, Hyperbound's AI assistant, what you want to see.** Upload your messaging guide, battlecard or launch brief, or type out up to three behaviors in priority order. Don't know where to start? Ask Kota to review your team's recent calls and surface the biggest gaps.
2. **Choose which calls count.** Narrow it by call type, a situation, a competitor, or words that come up on the call, so reps only hear about the moments that matter.
3. **Test it before anyone sees it.** Run it on past calls to see what would be counted, what would be missed, and the practice each rep would get. Nothing reaches a rep until you publish.
4. **Watch the dashboard.** See which reps are consistently showing each behavior, by week, team and rep, with every missed moment linked to the exact point in the call.
5. **Let it act on every miss.** Reps get written feedback on what the buyer said, what they missed and what to do instead, plus a short roleplay built for their next similar conversation, using the real stakeholder, company and scenario.


‍


‍


**Why it's different**


Conversation intelligence watches calls and stops at the report. Roleplay tools practice without ever seeing a real call. Initiatives measures and acts in one system: the missed moment on a real call becomes the practice.


And it's less work for enablement, not more. No tracker rules to write. No roleplays to build by hand. It even runs on calls you already record in other tools.


‍


## Six tips for a first initiative that lands


These apply whether you're using Initiatives or tracking a rollout another way. They come from our first design-partner sessions.


1. **Start with something you're already rolling out.** A new pitch, a product push, a battlecard. A dated rollout with a clear owner makes the best first initiative. "Sell better" doesn't.
2. **Write behaviors you could hear on a call.** Phrase each one as a question: "Did the rep ask about X?" Order them from "did they bring it up at all?" to "did they position it the right way?"
3. **Pick a trigger that actually comes up.** A competitor that appears on two calls a quarter won't give you enough data. Discovery calls, intro calls or a common objection will.
4. **Narrow the calls, not the ambition.** Reps already get feedback from every direction. Focus on the calls where the behavior should happen, so the feedback feels relevant, not like noise.
5. **Benchmark before you launch.** Look back at the last month of calls to see where the team stands on day one. Then you can show what changed, not just what happened.
6. **Pilot small, then expand.** Start with one rep or a handful, check what they'll receive, then roll it out to the team. Give it an end date: a week, a month or a quarter.


‍
